definition: The rate of change of velocity with time, $a = \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}s}{\mathrm{d}t^{2}} = v\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}s}$; in straight-line motion, a negative acceleration slows an object down only while its velocity is positive, because speed falls only when velocity and acceleration have opposite signs.

The total length of path an object covers between two times, counting motion in either direction, $\int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} \lvert v(t)\rvert\,\mathrm{d}t$; it equals the size of the displacement only if the object never changes direction in that time.
